THE PHASE-18 AUTHORITY CORRECTION IS THE SUBSTANCE OF THIS SUBJECT. An implementer had closed Phase 18 by typing `--to closed --delegated`: nothing was spoofed, the delegate's identity came from the plan, and every G4 predicate passed — the system simply had no representation of a DECISION, so eligibility was silently sufficient. Closure now requires a committed decision record naming the authority the plan records, for BOTH the owner and the delegated basis, and a read-only `phase closure-eligibility` command answers the question without performing the act.

THE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF THAT CORRECTION BROKE IT THREE MORE WAYS, all fixed at this subject and all regressed. Core did not defend itself: `transitionPhase` carved out `by === 'owner'`, so every protection lived in one caller and the Control Centre's project surface closed phases by calling core directly — core now demands an unforgeable grant for any closure. Decision replay via `phase new --force`, which erased the phase history the replay ledger lived in — consumption is now recorded in the decision itself and `--force` refuses a terminal phase. And a symlink defeated the committed check, because git was asked about the path while the bytes were read from the working tree — the decision is now read from the committed object with `git show`, so what is validated and what is committed are the same bytes.

Also fixed: owner grants omitted the decisionId, so no owner closure could ever be seen as consuming one; a caller-supplied `--note` could poison the replay ledger because the id was parsed by an unanchored search; and the implementer-identity filter folded with NFKC, which recomposes accents.
